news.headline: Dollar Tree (DLTR) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript
news.quote: Q3 comparable sales rose 4.6% and sales reached $5.1B; FY EPS guidance rises to $8.05-$8.25

touches.claim: Q2 profit was lifted by tariff refunds: diluted EPS of $2.70 included a $1.31 benefit, the operating margin gain included a 650 basis point refund benefit, and the full-year outlook still counts an approximate $0.60 refund benefit. Underlying earnings power is therefore smaller than the headline, and the refund boost may not repeat.

Traffic growth is thin and comparable sales growth depends mostly on average ticket. Q2 comps rose 3.7% with traffic up only 0.4%, and over six months traffic fell 0.3%. The 10-K said traffic declined in the last two quarters of fiscal 2025 after price changes. If price-led ticket growth fades, comps could slow.

Q3 results are due right after the decision time. The Q3 outlook has adjusted EPS of $0.80 to $0.95, including a $0.50 impact from tariff refund reinvestments, which sharply lowers the quarter's EPS from Q2's $2.70. A miss or a guide-down could change the reading of the year.
Dollar Tree is a scaled value retailer. It had 9,436 stores across the U.S. and Canada at the end of the second quarter of fiscal 2026, up from 9,282 at the start of the year.
Second-quarter sales growth was driven by both existing and new stores. Net sales rose 7.0% to $4,886.5 million, with comparable store net sales up 3.7%.
Customer traffic is only marginally positive. Q2 comparable sales rose on a 3.3% higher average ticket and 0.4% higher traffic, and traffic was down for the 26-week period.
The multi-price assortment is a differentiator that is being rolled out. About 710 stores were converted or added in Q2, ending the quarter with approximately 6,600 multi-price stores.

Management is reinvesting tariff refunds in the business, which dilutes near-term earnings. Q3 adjusted EPS guidance of $0.80 to $0.95 includes a $0.50 reinvestment impact, and full-year adjusted EPS guidance is $7.70 to $8.05.

Comparable store sales growth is a core driver. Q2 comps rose 3.7%, mostly from a 3.3% higher average ticket plus a 0.4% rise in traffic. For this to continue, traffic must hold up as ticket-raising pricing and mix changes are lapped.

Multi-price conversion is a driver of ticket and margin. The company converted or added about 710 stores in the quarter and ended with approximately 6,600 multi-price stores. For it to continue, customers must keep accepting prices above the $1.25 point, and labor and implementation costs must stay manageable.

Net new store and square-footage growth adds non-comparable sales. Stores rose to 9,436 from 9,148 a year earlier, and selling square footage grew 3.4%. Management plans approximately 400 openings and 75 closings this year. For this to continue, new sites must be found and opened on schedule at acceptable build-out cost.

Management guidance depends on the comp and margin conditions above: fiscal 2026 net sales of $20.5 billion to $20.7 billion on comps of 3% to 4%, and adjusted EPS of $7.70 to $8.05 including about $0.60 from net tariff refunds.

news.why: Dollar Tree beat Q3 FY2026 estimates with $5.1 billion in sales, 4.6% comparable sales growth, 3.8% traffic growth, 84 store openings, and easing multi-price backlash while raising full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $8.05-$8.25.

business_model.claim: Dollar Tree is a retail discount store operator, selling under the Dollar Tree and Dollar Tree Canada brands, and ended the third quarter with 9,511 stores.
quotes: We are a leading operator of retail discount stores operating under the brand names of Dollar Tree and Dollar Tree Canada.
Ended the quarter with 9,511 stores across the Dollar Tree U.S. and Dollar Tree Canada banners

business_model.claim: It sells consumable goods (household paper and chemicals, food, candy, health and personal care) and discretionary goods (variety and seasonal items). Basic everyday products are supplemented with seasonal, closeout and promotional merchandise.
quotes: We offer a wide selection of everyday basic products and we supplement these with seasonal, closeout and promotional merchandise.
Seasonal goods, which include, among others, Christmas, Easter, Halloween and Valentine’s Day merchandise.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited item; the evidence gives no finer customer breakdown
business_model.claim: The customers are retail shoppers with a broad range of income levels, served mainly from suburban store locations.
quotes: Our stores serve customers with a broad range of income levels principally in suburban locations and predominantly range from 8,000 - 10,000 selling square feet.

business_model.basis: stated in the cited items; no separate reporting segments are shown in the evidence
business_model.claim: The business reports on a continuing-operations basis covering the Dollar Tree U.S. and Dollar Tree Canada banners. The Family Dollar business was sold and is reported as discontinued operations. Canada is not material to revenue or assets.
quotes: The operating results of the Family Dollar business are reported as discontinued operations for all periods presented.
Our revenue and assets in Canada are not material.

business_model.claim: Third-quarter net sales rose 6.9% to $5,073.7 million. The growth came from a 4.6% comparable store sales increase plus $232.3 million of sales at non-comparable stores.
quotes: Net sales increased 6.9% to $5,073.7 million primarily due to a 4.6% comparable store net sales increase and net sales of $232.3 million at non-comparable stores.

business_model.claim: Comparable sales growth can come from traffic or from average ticket. In the third quarter, traffic rose 3.8% and ticket 0.8% for 4.6% comparable growth. In the prior fiscal year, comparable growth of 5.3% was mostly ticket (4.3%, with traffic 1.0%), driven by price changes and more multi-price items.
quotes: Comparable store net sales growth included a 3.8% increase in traffic and a 0.8% increase in average ticket
The increase in average ticket was primarily the result of targeted retail price changes executed during the second and third quarters of fiscal year 2025 and increased multi-price penetration.

business_model.claim: Pricing is anchored at $1.25, and the company is broadening it through a multi-price assortment. About 85% of products in the average store are priced at $2.00 or less. About 7,400 stores carry the multi-price format.
quotes: the majority of our products are priced at $1.25

Our multi-price strategy is designed to increase basket size and drive margin expansion by introducing complementary products, new categories, larger pack sizes, and select branded and licensed items that we could not historically offer under a single price point.
Converted or added approximately 800 stores to the Dollar Tree multi-price format, ending the quarter with approximately 7,400 multi-price stores

business_model.claim: Growth in store count is a second revenue driver. In the nine months the company opened 272 stores and closed 43, ending at 9,511. It guides to about 400 openings and 75 closings for the year.
quotes: Approximately 400 new store openings and 75 closings.

business_model.basis: stated in the income statement and release; the margin relationship is read directly from them
business_model.claim: In the third quarter, cost of sales and SG&A absorbed most of revenue: total revenue was 5,078.4, cost of sales 3,263.2, SG&A 1,517.0 and operating income 308.6 (table in millions). The gross margin was 35.7%, SG&A was 29.9% of revenue and operating margin was 6.1%.
quotes: Gross profit margin decreased 10 basis points to 35.7% and included 45 basis points of net cost from tariff refund reinvestment.
Operating income was $309 million and operating income margin was 6.1%.

business_model.claim: Merchandise cost is exposed to imports and tariffs. Directly imported goods are about 40% of retail-value purchases, China is the source of a vast majority of direct imports, and imported goods are described as carrying higher profit margins.
quotes: Among our foreign suppliers, China is the source of a vast majority of our direct imports and we believe that a significant portion of our goods purchased from domestic vendors is imported.
Imported goods are generally less expensive than domestic goods and result in higher profit margins.

business_model.claim: Operating costs are driven by store payroll and wages, depreciation, general liability claims and distribution and freight. The prior-year SG&A rate rose mainly because of store payroll tied to pricing initiatives and wage increases. Third-quarter gross profit growth was partly offset by higher product costs and domestic freight.
quotes: higher store payroll in support of our pricing initiatives and from wage increases

Gross profit increased 6.5% to $1,810.5 million primarily due to the 4.6% comparable store net sales increase and our net store growth, partially offset primarily by higher product costs, domestic freight cost increases and unfavorable sales mix.

business_model.claim: This year's margins are distorted by tariff refunds and their reinvestment. Nine-month gross profit margin of 38.4% includes a 210 basis point benefit from refunds net of reinvestment. The third quarter carried a 195 basis point operating margin cost from net tariff reinvestment.
quotes: Gross profit increased 16.5% to $5.7 billion and gross profit margin expanded 310 basis points to 38.4%, including a 210 basis point benefit from the net impact of tariff refunds and related reinvestments.
Operating income margin contracted 110 basis points including a 195 basis point cost related to the net impact of tariff reinvestments

business_model.claim: The business is seasonal. The fourth quarter produces a disproportionate share of net sales and income, and working capital needs peak in September and October.
quotes: we generally realize a disproportionate amount of our net sales and our operating and net income during the fourth quarter
Our working capital requirements for existing stores are seasonal in nature and typically reach their peak in the months of September and October.

financial_health.claim: Management says its funding sources cover its needs. Liquidity relies on operating cash flow, the commercial paper program and credit facilities, all of which are undrawn or unused at quarter-end.
quotes: We believe that we can adequately fund our working capital requirements and planned capital expenditures for the next 12 months and the foreseeable future from net cash provided by operations, our commercial paper program and borrowings under our credit facilities.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the conditions for continuation are inferred from the outlook and the 10-K MD&A.
growth_thesis.claim: Customer traffic is the main driver of recent comparable-store growth. Third-quarter comparable net sales rose 4.6%, with traffic up 3.8% and average ticket up 0.8%. For this to continue, traffic gains must hold, since management's fourth-quarter outlook assumes comparable growth of 3% to 4%.
quotes: Comparable store net sales increased 4.6%, driven by a 3.8% increase in traffic and a 0.8% increase in average ticket.

growth_thesis.basis: Store counts and outlook are stated in the cited items; the conditions are inferred from the risk factor text.
growth_thesis.claim: Net new stores add non-comparable sales, but the pace is slower than a year earlier. The company opened 272 stores in the 39 weeks, versus 360 a year earlier, and selling square footage grew 2.7% versus 5.4%. It plans approximately 400 openings and 75 closings for the year. For this to continue, it must keep finding and opening profitable sites.
quotes: net sales of $232.3 million at non-comparable stores
Approximately 400 new store openings and 75 closings.

growth_thesis.basis: Store counts are stated in the release; the mechanism is from the 10-K MD&A; the conditions are inferred from the risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: The multi-price assortment rollout is a stated growth lever. About 800 stores were converted or added in the quarter, ending with about 7,400 multi-price stores. For this to continue, customers must accept the broader assortment and the added labor and implementation costs must be recovered.
quotes: Converted or added approximately 800 stores to the Dollar Tree multi-price format, ending the quarter with approximately 7,400 multi-price stores

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release; the 10-K passage supports the uncertainty condition.
growth_thesis.claim: Tariff refunds are lifting the reported profit outlook, but they are being partly reinvested. Management raised its fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to $8.05 to $8.25, including an approximate $0.65 net benefit. In the third quarter the net tariff reinvestment cost $0.42 per share. For this to continue, the refunds must actually be received and the reinvestment must pay back in traffic and sales.
quotes: Increasing fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $8.05 to $8.25 including an approximate $0.65 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds

growth_thesis.basis: Figures are from the income and cash flow statements; the link between buybacks and EPS is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Per-share growth is being helped by a shrinking share count. Third-quarter diluted EPS rose to $1.24 from $1.20 even though income from continuing operations fell to $232.0 million from $244.6 million. Diluted shares fell to 187.6 million from 203.8 million. For this to continue, cash generation must keep funding buybacks.
quotes: The Company repurchased 12.9 million shares for $1.4 billion, excluding applicable excise tax.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the release and income statement; the leverage condition is inferred.
growth_thesis.claim: Margin leverage is a condition for converting sales growth into profit, and it did not hold in the third quarter. SG&A rose 70 basis points to 29.9% of total revenue, and operating income fell to 308.6 from 343.3 (income statement in millions) despite higher sales. For growth to reach earnings, SG&A growth must slow relative to sales.
quotes: Selling, general and administrative expenses increased 70 basis points to 29.9% of total revenue.

growth_thesis.basis: Stated in the 10-K; the dependency of growth on capacity is inferred from the risk factors.
growth_thesis.claim: Distribution capacity is the supply-side condition for store growth. The company is rebuilding the Marietta, Oklahoma distribution center, which is expected to serve approximately 700 stores in the West and Southwest. It must also bring the Phoenix site online without disrupting product availability.
quotes: In April 2025, we announced plans to return to Marietta, Oklahoma, with a new, enhanced distribution center expected to be fully operational by spring 2027, with capacity to serve approximately 700 stores across the West and Southwest regions.

material_events.claim: Dollar Tree completed the sale of the Family Dollar business, which is now reported as discontinued operations. It still provides services to Family Dollar under a transition services agreement.
quotes: On July 5, 2025, we completed our previously announced sale of the Family Dollar business to 1959 Holdings, LLC.

material_events.claim: In its third-quarter earnings release the company raised its full-year adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $8.05 to $8.25. The range includes a benefit of about $0.65 from net tariff refunds.
quotes: Increasing fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $8.05 to $8.25 including an approximate $0.65 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds

material_events.claim: The company recorded tariff refund reinvestment costs in the third quarter. These included a charitable donation inside selling, general and administrative expenses, and they were partly offset by IEEPA tariff refunds recorded in cost of sales.
quotes: Net impact of tariff reinvestments includes reinvestment expenses totaling $103 million including $27 million in cost of sales, $76 million in selling, general and administrative expenses, and IEEPA tariff refunds totaling $4 million in cost of sales.
SG&A included 150 basis points of tariff refund reinvestment, of which $40 million was attributable to a charitable donation.

material_events.claim: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled that certain IEEPA tariffs were unlawful. The company says it is acting to preserve its refund rights.
quotes: On February 20, 2026, the U.S. Supreme Court ruled that certain of the tariffs imposed last year under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act (“IEEPA”) were unlawful.

material_events.basis: stated in the cash flow statement; the link to the balance sheet change is inferred
material_events.claim: In the nine months ended October 31, 2026 the company received proceeds from long-term debt of 500.0 (table in millions). Net long-term debt rose over the same period.
quotes: Proceeds from long-term debt | 500.0 | 0.0

risks.basis: Stated in the income statement and the earnings release; the mechanism is inferred from the release's attribution of the margin decline.
risks.claim: Q3 operating income fell to 308.6 (table in millions) from 343.3, and operating margin contracted 110 basis points, including a 195 basis point cost from tariff refund reinvestments. SG&A rose to 29.9% of revenue.
quotes: Operating income margin contracted 110 basis points including a 195 basis point cost related to the net impact of tariff reinvestments

risks.basis: The guidance wording is stated in the release. The risk to recurring earnings is inferred from the size of the refund item in the outlook.
risks.claim: Full-year adjusted EPS guidance includes about $0.65 from net tariff refunds. Earnings quality and the sustainability of profit depend on refund-related items rather than recurring operations.
quotes: Increasing fiscal 2026 adjusted EPS outlook to a range of $8.05 to $8.25 including an approximate $0.65 benefit related to the net impact of tariff refunds
there remains substantial uncertainty regarding the impacts of this decision on the availability, timing, and amount of potential refunds, if any, for the invalidated tariffs

risks.basis: Stated in the 10-K risk factors and MD&A. The 10-K is dated March 2026, so it may not reflect the latest tariff status.
risks.claim: Tariff and trade policy remains a cost and supply risk. Directly imported goods are about 40% of purchases, and the company expects tariff volatility to persist.
quotes: We expect tariff volatility to persist in the near-term, and implementation costs associated with our mitigation strategies may continue to be experienced before the benefits from those efforts are expected to materialize.

risks.basis: Guidance and Q3 figures are stated. The deceleration is read from the two figures. The easier-comparison point is inferred from the 10-K.
risks.claim: Q4 comparable-store sales growth is guided to 3% to 4%, below the 4.6% reported for Q3. The comp gain in Q3 came mostly from traffic, with only a small average-ticket gain.
quotes: Q4 fiscal 2026 outlook of 3% to 4% comparable store net sales growth and adjusted EPS of $2.46 to $2.66 including an approximate $0.25 cost related to tariff refund reinvestments

risks.basis: Balance sheet and cash flow figures are stated. The risk framing is inferred and is a low-probability reading.
risks.claim: Debt-funded buybacks and working-capital-aided cash flow raise leverage. Long-term debt, net rose to 2,934.4 (table in millions) from 2,431.7 after 500.0 of debt proceeds, while 1,414.7 went to share repurchases over nine months.
quotes: no commercial paper outstanding, and no borrowings under its revolving credit facility

risks.basis: The agreement term and income figures are stated. The end date is inferred from the sale date.
risks.claim: Transition services agreement income from Family Dollar is shrinking. Q3 was 10.4 (table in millions) versus 23.8 a year earlier, and the agreement runs for a fixed term.
quotes: The Company has continuing involvement with Family Dollar under a transition services agreement, through which the Company and Family Dollar continue to provide certain services to each other for a period of 18 months following the date of sale.

thesis_change.claim: Comparable store net sales rose 4.6% in the third quarter, with traffic up 3.8% and average ticket up 0.8%. Growth is now led by traffic rather than ticket, so the earlier concern about traffic holding up as pricing is lapped is partly answered.
quotes: Comparable store net sales growth included a 3.8% increase in traffic and a 0.8% increase in average ticket

thesis_change.basis: Stated in the earnings release; the comparison to the earlier count comes from the earlier point.

quotes: Converted or added approximately 800 stores to the Dollar Tree multi-price format, ending the quarter with approximately 7,400 multi-price stores

thesis_change.basis: Stated in the release's store activity table and outlook.

quotes: Approximately 400 new store openings and 75 closings.

thesis_change.basis: Stated in the 10-Q MD&A and the release.
thesis_change.claim: Third-quarter gross profit rose 6.5% to $1,810.5 million, and gross margin fell 10 basis points to 35.7%. That included 45 basis points of net cost from tariff refund reinvestment, so refunds were a net cost this quarter. The nine-month margin still includes a 210 basis point benefit from net refunds and reinvestments.
quotes: Gross profit margin decreased 10 basis points to 35.7% and included 45 basis points of net cost from tariff refund reinvestment.

thesis_change.basis: Stated in the income statement and the release.
thesis_change.claim: Third-quarter diluted weighted average shares were 187.6 versus 203.8 a year earlier (shares in millions). The company repurchased stock for $205 million in the quarter and has $2.3 billion remaining under its authorization.
quotes: The Company repurchased 1.8 million shares of its common stock during the third quarter of fiscal 2026 for $205 million, excluding applicable excise tax.

thesis_change.basis: Stated in the cash flow statement.
thesis_change.claim: Nine-month net cash from continuing operations was 1,940.8 versus 958.5 a year earlier, with capital expenditures of 752.5 (table in millions). The figure includes an accounts payable inflow of 336.2 and a deferred tax provision of 236.4.

thesis_change.basis: Inferred from the absence of project-specific detail in the cited items.

The full-year outlook was raised: net sales of $20.6 billion to $20.7 billion on comps of 3.5% to 4.0%, and adjusted EPS of $8.05 to $8.25 including approximately $0.65 from net tariff refunds and reinvestment.
quotes: Adjusted diluted EPS of $8.05 to $8.25, including approximately $0.65 related to the net impact of tariff refunds and tariff refund reinvestments.

thesis_change.basis: Stated in the release and income statement.
thesis_change.claim: In the third quarter diluted EPS of $1.24 included a $0.42 cost from net tariff reinvestments, reversing the second-quarter benefit. Nine-month diluted EPS of $5.70 includes a $0.90 net benefit, and the full-year outlook counts approximately $0.65 of benefit. The headline-versus-underlying gap persists but is smaller for the full year.
quotes: Diluted EPS of $1.24, including $0.42 of cost related to the net impact of tariff reinvestments

quotes: The direct and indirect impacts of and challenges associated with the current and potential tariff environment

thesis_change.claim: Traffic is no longer thin. Third-quarter traffic rose 3.8% and comps 4.6%. Over nine months traffic rose 1.1% and average ticket 2.9%.
quotes: Comparable store net sales increased 4.0%, reflecting a 2.9% increase in average ticket and a 1.1% increase in traffic.

thesis_change.claim: The third-quarter report is now out: diluted EPS was $1.24 and adjusted EPS $1.16. The fourth-quarter outlook is adjusted EPS of $2.46 to $2.66 including an approximate $0.25 cost from tariff refund reinvestments.
